parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the stretching of a spring. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The metre rule is clamped in position near to the spring. Do not change the position of the metre rule.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Use the set square provided to take readings from the metre rule to determine the unstretched length L of the coiled part of the spring. Record the value of L . L = ...................................................mm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Draw a diagram to show clearly how you used the set square to obtain an accurate reading from the metre rule. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: clear diagram showing horizontal line of set square across to metre rule

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • Suspend a load P = 0.20 N on the spring. Record in Table 1.1 the new length l of the spring. • Repeat the procedure using loads P = 0.40 N, 0.60 N, 0.80 N and 1.00 N. Table 1.1 P / N l / mm 0.20 0.40 0.60 0.80 1.00 [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of l / mm ( y -axis) against P / N ( x -axis). Start both axes at the origin (0,0). [4]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
graph:
axes correctly labelled and right way round
suitable scales
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The intercept on the y -axis of the graph is numerically equal to the length l 0 of the spring when P = 0. Determine the value of l 0 . Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. l 0 = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
intercept method clearly shown
l0 value correctly read to ½ small square
